direct_prompt: The phone in Eleanor Briggs’s small kitchen rang for the third time that morning, just as she was settling down with her crossword. She checked the caller ID, saw an unfamiliar number, and answered anyway, because at ninety-two she considered every voice a possible visit. “Hello?” she said, voice thin but steady. There was a pause, a breath, then a young man’s trembling whisper: “H–Hello, is this… is this the hotline?” “No, dear, this is Eleanor’s kitchen,” she replied. “But you sound like you need someone to talk to.” The silence on the other end stretched, then cracked into a sob. “I—I dialed the wrong number,” he managed. “I’m sorry, I’ll just—” “You called a human being, didn’t you?” she interrupted gently. “Wrong numbers are still numbers; you’ve got me now.” He didn’t hang up. “I don’t know what to do anymore,” he said. “I think I’m done.” “Oh, honey,” Eleanor said, pushing her untouched crossword aside. “Sit tight; we’ll untangle that sentence together.” She listened more than she spoke, asked questions instead of offering solutions, and every so often made soft little noises so he knew she was still there.

direct_prompt: The bullet hovered a breath from his forehead, its metal skin shimmering with stolen motion. He stared at it, pupils dilated, mind sprinting while the world refused to move. On the couch behind him, his sister’s laughter was frozen mid-spark, lips parted around a joke he would now never hear. He realized, with an oddly clinical calm, that he had never noticed the exact shade of brown in her eyes, captured now in perfect, terrified clarity. The shooter’s finger trembled against the trigger, but it was the trembling of a statue, intention without time to complete itself. Somewhere beneath his ribs, a surge of regret rose and crystallized, unable to become a sigh, a plea, a final word. He thought—not in sequence, not as a chain, but as a single bursting star—of the text he hadn’t answered, the apology his pride had smothered, the life he had worn like a shirt he meant to change someday.

title: Learning to Bluff
human_text: The act of bluffing confounds game designers to this day. The very nature ofbluffing is even open for debate, adding further complication to the process ofcreating intelligent virtual players that can bluff, and hence play,realistically. Through the use of intelligent, learning agents, and carefullydesigned agent outlooks, an agent can in fact learn to predict its opponentsreactions based not only on its own cards, but on the actions of those aroundit. With this wider scope of understanding, an agent can in learn to bluff itsopponents, with the action representing not an illogical action, as bluffing isoften viewed, but rather as an act of maximising returns through an effectivestatistical optimisation. By using a tee dee lambda learning algorithm tocontinuously adapt neural network agent intelligence, agents have been shown tobe able to learn to bluff without outside prompting, and even to learn to calleach others bluffs in free, competitive play.
direct_prompt: In strategic environments characterized by incomplete information, the ability to deceive opponents through bluffing is essential for maximizing long-term utility. This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning framework designed to autonomously optimize deceptive tactics within competitive multi-agent simulations. By leveraging counterfactual regret minimization, the agent learns to calibrate its betting patterns to exploit opponent weaknesses while remaining strategically unpredictable. Empirical evaluations across multiple poker variants demonstrate that the model successfully achieves equilibrium strategies that outperform standard heuristic-based benchmarks. Ultimately, this research provides critical insights into the computational mechanisms of strategic deception, with broader applications in automated negotiation and cybersecurity.

human_text: Jesus, welcome to my world. My mother was dying from cancer when I was 12. Abandoned by every adult, she put me in charge of her medications. I only wanted to help. She died the next morning. 6 months later I told my father how happy I was that he was doing something good for himself, though he abandoned our sick mother. He' d been pretty selfish, but I only wanted to help. A few hours later he died of a heart attack from a heroine overdose. I lived with my brother after that. My brother refused to send me to a military school out of guilt. I did everything possible to be invisible. I only wanted to help. A couple of months later, his husband died drinking himself to death because my brother chose me over him. My brother fell into a deep alcoholic depression. I knew I could n' t be his burden any longer. I went back to my home town to live with friends of the family as their adoptive son. I had my best friend from elementary in my corner helping me. Dropping me off before church, he is side-swiped by a truck. I see the life fade from him. This is labeled by everyone in a God-fearing small town as my fault. I only wanted to help. Years have gone by. I' m 30 now. The friends I' ve made, the family I' ve built... It does n' t matter. They' v moved forward with their lives. I only wanted to help. ( A true story )
direct_prompt: I discovered my curse on my seventh birthday when I helped Mrs. Henderson carry her groceries up the stairs. She thanked me with a warm smile, ruffled my hair, and collapsed dead on her doorstep twenty minutes later. The doctors called it a sudden heart attack, a tragic coincidence that no one could have predicted. But when my teacher Miss Roberts died the day after I brought her flowers for her birthday, I began to suspect something terrible. The pattern became undeniable as more deaths followed my acts of kindness—the mailman who received my homemade cookies, the librarian I helped organize books, the elderly man whose dropped wallet I returned. I tried to convince myself it was all in my head, that correlation didn't equal causation. Yet every gesture of goodwill I extended became someone's final memory, every smile I shared became their last glimpse of human warmth. By age sixteen, I had become a hermit, avoiding all human contact to protect the world from my toxic compassion. I watched through my window as neighbors struggled with heavy packages, fought every instinct to help, and died a little inside with each ignored opportunity for kindness. My parents had died when I offered to make them breakfast in bed on Mother's and Father's Day—a double tragedy that confirmed my worst fears. The guilt consumed me like acid, eating away at my soul until I felt hollow and monstrous.

"I am Death," he said simply, stepping inside without invitation, "and I have a proposition for you." Marina, surprisingly unafraid, gestured to the chess set on her table. "I suppose you want to play for my soul, like in the old stories?" Death smiled—a cold, thin expression—and shook his head. "Quite the opposite, actually. I want you to teach me to play properly, and in exchange, I'll give you fifty additional years of life." The offer hung in the air like morning mist as Marina processed his words. "Why me?" she asked, settling into her chair across from him. "I've been playing for millennia," Death explained, "but I always lose to the great masters when their time comes. It's becoming rather embarrassing." Marina laughed despite herself, realizing that Death's pride was wounded by centuries of defeats. "What makes you think I'll be any different as a teacher than your previous opponents were as players?" Death leaned forward, his eyes gleaming with ancient frustration.

title: Enhanced spin-orbit scattering length in narrow Al_xGa_{1-x}N/GaN wires
human_text: The magnetotransport in a set of identical parallel AlGaN/GaN quantum wirestructures was investigated. The width of the wires was ranging between 1110 nmand 340 nm. For all sets of wires clear Shubnikov--de Haas oscillations areobserved. For the wider quantum wires the weak antilocalization effect isclearly observed, indicating the presence of spin-orbit coupling. title: Search for gravitational-wave bursts in LIGO data from the fourth  science run
human_text: The fourth science run of the LIGO and GEO 600 gravitational-wave detectors,carried out in early 2005, collected data with significantly lower noise thanprevious science runs. We report on a search for short-durationgravitational-wave bursts with arbitrary waveform in the 64-1600 Hz frequencyrange appearing in all three LIGO interferometers. Signal consistency tests,data quality cuts, and auxiliary-channel vetoes are applied to reduce the rateof spurious triggers. No gravitational-wave signals are detected in 15.5 daysof live observation time; we set a frequentist upper limit of 0.15 per day (at90% confidence level) on the rate of bursts with large enough amplitudes to bedetected reliably. The amplitude sensitivity of the search, characterized usingMonte Carlo simulations, is several times better than that of previoussearches. We also provide rough estimates of the distances at whichrepresentative supernova and binary black hole merger signals could be detectedwith 50% efficiency by this analysis.
direct_prompt: We present a search for unmodeled gravitational-wave bursts in data collected by the LIGO detectors during the fourth science run (S4). The analysis targets short-duration (≲1 s) transient signals over a broad frequency band, with minimal assumptions about waveform morphology or source population. Data from the three LIGO interferometers were coherently analyzed using a network burst pipeline that incorporates data-quality vetoes, coincidence requirements, and consistency tests to suppress instrumental and environmental artifacts. No gravitational-wave burst candidates with a significance above the estimated background were identified in the S4 data set. In the absence of a detection, we set frequentist upper limits on the rate of gravitational-wave bursts as a function of signal amplitude and frequency, and we translate these into constraints on selected astrophysical source models. These results demonstrate improved sensitivity over previous runs and help define the prospects for detecting gravitational-wave bursts in subsequent, more sensitive LIGO observing campaigns.

title: A Note on the Inapproximability of Correlation Clustering
human_text: We consider inapproximability of the correlation clustering problem definedas follows: Given a graph $G = (V,E)$ where each edge is labeled either "+"(similar) or "-" (dissimilar), correlation clustering seeks to partition thevertices into clusters so that the number of pairs correctly (resp.incorrectly) classified with respect to the labels is maximized (resp.minimized). The two complementary problems are called MaxAgree and MinDisagree,respectively, and have been studied on complete graphs, where every edge islabeled, and general graphs, where some edge might not have been labeled.Natural edge-weighted versions of both problems have been studied as well. LetS-MaxAgree denote the weighted problem where all weights are taken from set S,we show that S-MaxAgree with weights bounded by $O(|V|^{1/2-\delta})$essentially belongs to the same hardness class in the following sense: if thereis a polynomial time algorithm that approximates S-MaxAgree within a factor of$\lambda = O(\log{|V|})$ with high probability, then for any choice of S',S'-MaxAgree can be approximated in polynomial time within a factor of $(\lambda+ \epsilon)$, where $\epsilon > 0$ can be arbitrarily small, with highprobability. A similar statement also holds for $S-MinDisagree. This resultimplies it is hard (assuming $NP \neq RP$) to approximate unweighted MaxAgreewithin a factor of $80/79-\epsilon$, improving upon a previous known factor of$116/115-\epsilon$ by Charikar et. al. \cite{Chari05}.
direct_prompt: This note addresses the computational complexity inherent in correlation clustering, focusing specifically on its inapproximability aspects. Correlation clustering involves partitioning data points based on pairwise similarity or dissimilarity, with applications spanning data mining, machine learning, and network analysis. Despite extensive research on approximation algorithms, fundamental hardness results limit the quality of achievable solutions. We provide a concise treatment of existing inapproximability bounds, highlighting conditions under which no polynomial-time algorithm can approximate correlation clustering within certain factors unless widely accepted complexity assumptions fail. Our analysis sharpens the known hardness thresholds by leveraging reductions from well-studied combinatorial optimization problems. Furthermore, we discuss the implications of these results for practical algorithm design, emphasizing the trade-offs between computational feasibility and solution accuracy. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the theoretical limitations that govern correlation clustering and guides future exploration of algorithmic strategies under structural constraints.

title: On the change of latitude of Arctic East Siberia at the end of the  Pleistocene
human_text: Mammoths lived in Arctic East Siberia. In this region there is not sufficientsunlight over the year for the growth of the plants on which these animalsfeed. Therefore the latitude of this region was lower before the end of thePleistocene. As the cause of this geographic pole shift, we postulate a massiveobject, which moved in an extremely eccentric orbit and was hot from tidal workand solar radiation. Evaporation produced a disk-shaped cloud of ions aroundthe Sun. This cloud partially shielded the solar radiation, producing the coldand warm periods that characterize the Pleistocene. The shielding depends onthe inclination of Earth's orbit, which has a period of 100'000 years. Thecloud builds up to a density at which inelastic particle collisions induce itscollapse The resulting near-periodic time dependence resembles that ofDansgaard-Oeschger events. title: Spheroidal and torsional modes of quasistatic shear oscillations in the  solid globe models of nuclear physics and pulsar astrophysics
human_text: The past three decades of investigation on nuclear physics and pulsarastrophysics have seen gradual recognition that elastodynamic approach to thecontinuum mechanics of nuclear matter provides proper account of macroscopicmotions of degenerate Fermi-matter constituting interior of the nuclearmaterial objects, the densest of all known today. This paper focuses on onetheoretical issue of this development which is concerned with oscillatorybehavior of a viscoelastic solid globe in the regime of quasistatic,force-free, non-compressional oscillations less investigated in the literaturecompared to oscillations in the regime of standing shear waves. We show that inthis case the problem of computing frequency and lifetime of spheroidal andtorsional modes of non-radial shear vibrations damped by viscosity can beunambiguously resolved by working from the energy balance equation and takingadvantage of the Rayleigh's variational method. The efficiency of this methodis demonstrated by solid globe models of nuclear physics and pulsarastrophysics dealing with oscillations of a spherical mass of a viscoelasticFermi-solid with homogeneous and non-homogeneous profiles of the bulk density,the shear modulus, and the shear viscosity.
direct_prompt: We investigate spheroidal and torsional modes of quasistatic shear oscillations in solid globe models relevant to both nuclear physics and pulsar astrophysics. Employing a continuum-mechanical framework with appropriate elastic and boundary conditions, we derive analytical expressions for the eigenfrequencies and eigenfunctions of these modes. The resulting spectral characteristics are examined for their dependence on material parameters and geometrical scales typical of nuclear matter distributions and neutron star interiors. title: Dynamics of light propagation in spatiotemporal dielectric structures

Transfer matrices of sharp nonstationary interfacesare calculated explicitly, together with the amplitudes of all secondary wavesproduced in the scattering. Time-varying multilayer structures andspatiotemporal lenses in various configurations are investigated analyticallyand numerically in a unified approach. title: Rythmes d'activit\'e locomotrice chez deux insectes parasito\"ides  sympatriques : Eupelmus orientalis et Eupelmus vuilleti (Hym\'enopt\`ere,  Eupelmidae)
human_text: With an automatic image analysis device, we studied the temporal distributionof the locomotor activity of E. orientalis and E. vuilleti during 24 h, andover several days to know whether the activity rhythms of these two Eupelmidaeplay a role in their competitive interactions. These two Eupelmidaehave similar activity rhythms. Displacements of these parasitoids essentiallytake place during the photophase. But the activity of E. vuilleti is earlier,because the individuals of this species start their activity on average 4 to 5h earlier than those of E. orientalis. E. vuilleti begins its displacementsseveral hours before the onset of lighting, whereas E. orientalis is activeonly in the presence of the light. This shift of starting activity is thus afactor allowing these concurrent species to minimize their interactions duringthe cohabitation period in traditional granaries after the harvests of cowpea.

Chez les insectes parasitoïdes, les rythmes circadiens d'activité jouent un rôle clé dans la coexistence interspécifique, notamment en raison de la difficulté à reconnaître les hôtes déjà parasités par une espèce congénérique. La présente étude examine la répartition temporelle de l'activité locomotrice de ces deux espèces à l'échelle journalière et sur plusieurs jours. À l'aide d'un dispositif automatique d'analyse d'images, les enregistrements montrent que l'activité locomotrice des deux espèces présente des variations cycliques journalières synchronisées sur le cycle photopériodique. Les déplacements ont lieu essentiellement pendant la photophase, indiquant un rythme diurne marqué chez les deux parasitoïdes. Néanmoins, E. vuilleti initie son activité plus tôt, avec un début moyen 4 à 5 heures avant celui d'E. orientalis, et peut même commencer à se déplacer avant l'aube.

title: Energy-Efficient Resource Allocation in Wireless Networks with  Quality-of-Service Constraints
human_text: A game-theoretic model is proposed to study the cross-layer problem of jointpower and rate control with quality of service (QoS) constraints inmultiple-access networks. In the proposed game, each user seeks to choose itstransmit power and rate in a distributed manner in order to maximize its ownutility while satisfying its QoS requirements. The user's QoS constraints arespecified in terms of the average source rate and an upper bound on the averagedelay where the delay includes both transmission and queuing delays. Theutility function considered here measures energy efficiency and is particularlysuitable for wireless networks with energy constraints. The Nash equilibriumsolution for the proposed non-cooperative game is derived and a closed-formexpression for the utility achieved at equilibrium is obtained. It is shownthat the QoS requirements of a user translate into a "size" for the user whichis an indication of the amount of network resources consumed by the user. Usingthis competitive multiuser framework, the tradeoffs among throughput, delay,network capacity and energy efficiency are studied. In addition, analyticalexpressions are given for users' delay profiles and the delay performance ofthe users at Nash equilibrium is quantified.
direct_prompt: The exponential growth of mobile data traffic has necessitated the development of more sustainable and energy-efficient communication infrastructures. However, achieving high energy efficiency often conflicts with the strict quality-of-service (QoS) requirements demanded by modern low-latency applications. This paper investigates the problem of joint power allocation and subchannel assignment to maximize network energy efficiency while satisfying heterogeneous QoS constraints. We formulate this challenge as a non-convex optimization problem that accounts for delay sensitivity, interference limitations, and minimum throughput thresholds. To solve the problem effectively, a low-complexity iterative algorithm based on fractional programming and Lagrangian dual decomposition is proposed. Extensive numerical simulations are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed framework across diverse network deployment scenarios. The results demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances energy efficiency compared to traditional resource allocation schemes without sacrificing user throughput. Ultimately, these findings provide critical insights for the design of next-generation green wireless networks that prioritize both environmental sustainability and service reliability.

direct_prompt: Asteroid deflection represents a critical component of planetary defense against potentially hazardous near-Earth objects (NEOs). The threat of asteroid impacts has motivated extensive research into mitigation strategies. This review examines the primary methods for deflecting asteroids, the optimal locations for intervention, and the necessary timelines for effective action. Kinetic impactors involve deliberately colliding a spacecraft with an asteroid to alter its trajectory via momentum transfer. NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission successfully demonstrated this technique in 2022 by impacting Dimorphos. The DART impact shortened Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by approximately 32 minutes, exceeding expectations due to ejecta enhancement. Gravity tractors utilize the mutual gravitational attraction between a spacecraft and an asteroid to slowly tug it off course. This contactless method is particularly suitable for rubble-pile asteroids, avoiding fragmentation risks. Ion beam shepherds and laser ablation offer alternative slow-push techniques by directing focused energy to sublimate surface material. Nuclear standoff explosions provide high-energy deflection for large asteroids or short-warning scenarios, though they carry political and fragmentation challenges. The choice of deflection method depends on asteroid size, composition, spin rate, and available lead time. Intervention is most effective when applied along the asteroid's velocity vector, far from Earth to maximize orbital deviation. Gravitational keyholes—narrow regions where Earth's gravity could redirect an asteroid toward future impact—must be avoided during deflection.

title: Principal Component Analysis and Automatic Relevance Determination in  Damage Identification
human_text: This paper compares two neural network input selection schemes, the PrincipalComponent Analysis (PCA) and the Automatic Relevance Determination (ARD) basedon Mac-Kay's evidence framework. The PCA takes all the input data and projectsit onto a lower dimension space, thereby reduc-ing the dimension of the inputspace. This input reduction method often results with parameters that havesignificant influence on the dynamics of the data being diluted by those thatdo not influence the dynamics of the data. The ARD selects the most relevantinput parameters and discards those that do not contribute significantly to thedynamics of the data being modelled. The ARD sometimes results with importantinput parameters being discarded thereby compromising the dynamics of the data.The PCA and ARD methods are implemented together with a Multi-Layer-Perceptron(MLP) network for fault identification in structures and the performance of thetwo methods is as-sessed. It is observed that ARD and PCA give similaraccu-racy levels when used as input-selection schemes. There-fore, the choiceof input-selection scheme is dependent on the nature of the data beingprocessed.
direct_prompt: This study compares the effectiveness of Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Automatic Relevance Determination (ARD) as input selection techniques for neural network-based structural damage identification. PCA is employed to reduce the dimensionality of measured vibration data, such as frequency response functions, by projecting the inputs onto a lower-dimensional space that captures the principal modes of variation. In contrast, ARD, grounded in Mackay's Bayesian evidence framework, automatically identifies and retains only the most relevant input parameters while pruning those with negligible contribution to the modeled dynamics. The two approaches are integrated with a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) neural network to classify and identify structural faults using experimental data from benchmark structures. Results demonstrate that while PCA effectively compresses the input space, it may dilute the influence of critical damage-sensitive features by including less relevant components. ARD provides a more selective input representation, though it occasionally discards parameters important to the damage dynamics. Overall, the comparison highlights the trade-offs between dimensionality reduction and feature relevance in enhancing the accuracy and robustness of damage detection in.

title: Collective excitations of hard-core Bosons at half filling on square and  triangular lattices: Development of roton minima and collapse of roton gap
human_text: We study ground state properties and excitation spectra for hard-core Bosonson square and triangular lattices, at half filling, using series expansionmethods. Nearest-neighbor repulsion between the Bosons leads to the developmentof short-range density order at the antiferromagnetic wavevector, andsimultaneously a roton minima in the density excitation spectra. On thesquare-lattice, the model maps on to the well studied XXZ model, and the rotongap collapses to zero precisely at the Heisenberg symmetry point, leading tothe well known spectra for the Heisenberg antiferromagnet. On thetriangular-lattice, the collapse of the roton gap signals the onset of thesupersolid phase. Our results suggest that the transition from the superfluidto the supersolid phase maybe weakly first order. We also find several featuresin the density of states, including two-peaks and a sharp discontinuity, whichmaybe observable in experimental realization of such systems.
direct_prompt: We investigate the collective excitation spectra of hard‑core Bosons at half filling on both square and triangular lattices, with particular emphasis on the emergence and evolution of roton minima. Using a combination of linear spin‑wave theory, numerical exact diagonalization, and series expansion techniques, we map out the dispersion relations as a function of interaction strength and lattice geometry. On the square lattice, we find that increasing nearest‑neighbor repulsion leads to the progressive softening of excitations at specific momenta, resulting in well‑defined roton minima in the dynamic structure factor. For the frustrated triangular lattice, the roton features are more pronounced and appear over a broader region of parameter space, reflecting the enhanced role of quantum fluctuations. We demonstrate that upon approaching critical interaction strengths, the roton gap collapses, signaling an instability toward density‑wave or supersolid ordering depending on the lattice and parameter regime.

title: Photo-z for weak lensing tomography from space: the role of optical and  near-IR photometry
human_text: We study in detail the photometric redshift requirements needed fortomographic weak gravitational lensing in order to measure accurately the DarkEnergy equation of state. In particular, we examine how ground-based photometry(u,g,r,i,z,y) can be complemented by space-based near-infrared (IR) photometry(J,H), e.g. on board the planned DUNE satellite. Using realistic photometricredshift simulations and an artificial neural network photo-z method weevaluate the Figure of Merit for the Dark Energy parameters $(w_0, w_a)$. Weconsider a DUNE-like broad optical filter supplemented with ground-basedmulti-band optical data from surveys like the Dark Energy Survey, Pan-STARRSand LSST. We show that the Dark Energy Figure of Merit would improved by afactor of 1.3 to 1.7 if IR filters are added on board DUNE. Furthermore we showthat with IR data catastrophic photo-z outliers can be removed effectively.There is an interplay between the choice of filters, the magnitude limits andthe removal of outliers. We draw attention to the dependence of the results onthe galaxy formation scenarios encoded into the mock galaxies, e.g the galaxyreddening. For example, deep u band data could be as effective as the IR. Wealso find that about $10^5-10^6$ spectroscopic redshifts are needed forcalibration of the full survey.
direct_prompt: Accurate photometric redshifts (photo-z) are essential for tomographic weak gravitational lensing surveys from space, enabling the division of galaxies into redshift bins to probe the evolution of cosmic structures. This study investigates the photometric redshift requirements for precisely constraining the dark energy equation of state parameters. Ground-based multi-band optical photometry in filters such as u, g, r, i, z, and y provides a baseline for photo-z estimation. Space-based observations complement these with a broad optical filter and near-infrared (near-IR) bands like J and H. Realistic simulations of galaxy catalogs are employed to mimic future space missions and ground-based surveys. An artificial neural network method is used to compute photometric redshifts from the simulated multi-band data. The dark energy figure of merit is evaluated for parameters w₀ and wₐ across various filter combinations and depth scenarios. Adding space-based near-IR photometry significantly reduces photo-z scatter and catastrophic outliers compared to optical-only data. The improvement in the dark energy figure of merit ranges from a factor of 1.3 to 1.7 when near-IR filters are included. Deep u-band observations from the ground can alternatively mitigate outliers by distinguishing reddened galaxies, though near-IR data proves more robust across magnitude limits.

title: Impact of spin-zero particle-photon interactions on light polarization  in external magnetic fields
human_text: If the recent PVLAS results on polarization changes of a linearly polarizedlaser beam passing through a magnetic field are interpreted by an axion-likeparticle, it is almost certain that it is not a standard QCD axion. Consideringthis, we study the general effective interactions of photons with spin-zeroparticles without restricting the latter to be a pseudo-scalar or a scalar,i.e., a parity eigenstate. At the lowest order in effective field theory, thereare two dimension-5 interactions, each of which has previously been treatedseparately for a pseudo-scalar or a scalar particle. By following the evolutionin an external magnetic field of the system of spin-zero particles and photons,we compute the changes in light polarization and the transition probability fortwo experimental set-ups: one-way propagation and round-trip propagation. Whilethe first may be relevant for astrophysical sources of spin-zero particles, thesecond applies to laboratory optical experiments like PVLAS. In the one-waypropagation, interesting phenomena can occur for special configurations ofpolarization where, for instance, transition occurs but light polarization doesnot change. For the round-trip propagation, however, the standard results ofpolarization changes for a pseudoscalar or a scalar are only modified by afactor that depends on the relative strength of the two interactions.
direct_prompt: This study investigates the influence of spin-zero particle-photon interactions on the polarization state of light propagating through external magnetic fields. We develop a theoretical framework that incorporates axion-like particle couplings to photons, allowing for the analysis of polarization rotation and ellipticity induced by such interactions. Our model predicts measurable deviations from classical magneto-optical effects under experimentally accessible conditions. We perform numerical simulations over a range of magnetic field strengths and particle coupling parameters to identify signatures characteristic of spin-zero particle influence. The results indicate potential enhancements in polarization rotation angle corresponding to specific coupling regimes. These findings have implications for laboratory experiments seeking to detect light pseudoscalar particles via polarimetric techniques. Finally, we discuss prospects for improving sensitivity in upcoming searches and suggest experimental setups optimized to probe these subtle quantum effects.

title: On Lagrangian submanifolds in complex hyperquadrics and isoparametric  hypersurfaces in spheres
human_text: The $n$-dimensional complex hyperquadric is a compact complex algebraichypersurface defined by the quadratic equation in the $(n+1)$-dimensionalcomplex projective space, which is isometric to the real Grassmann manifold oforiented 2- planes and is a compact Hermitian symmetric space of rank 2. Inthis paper we study geometry of compact Lagrangian submanifolds in complexhyperquadrics from the viewpoint of the theory of isoparametric hypersurfacesin spheres. From this viewpoint we provide a classification theorem of compacthomogeneous Lagrangian submanifolds in complex hyperquadrics by using themoment map technique. Moreover we determine the Hamiltonian stability ofcompact minimal Lagrangian submanifolds embedded in complex hyperquadrics whichare obtained as Gauss images of isoparametric hypersurfaces in spheres with$g(=1,2,3)$ distinct principal curvatures.
direct_prompt: This paper investigates the geometric correspondence between Lagrangian submanifolds in complex hyperquadrics and the class of isoparametric hypersurfaces in unit spheres. By employing the Gauss map of an isoparametric hypersurface, we construct specific examples of Lagrangian submanifolds and analyze their embedding properties within the Kähler setting. We demonstrate that several important classes of Lagrangian submanifolds, including those that are Hamiltonian minimal or H-umbilic, naturally arise from the principal curvature data of these hypersurfaces. These findings provide a unified framework for classifying certain Lagrangian submanifolds and offer new insights into the symmetry groups and variational problems of complex hyperquadrics.

title: Many Random Walks Are Faster Than One
human_text: We pose a new and intriguing question motivated by distributed computingregarding random walks on graphs: How long does it take for several independentrandom walks, starting from the same vertex, to cover an entire graph? We studythe cover time - the expected time required to visit every node in a graph atleast once - and we show that for a large collection of interesting graphs,running many random walks in parallel yields a speed-up in the cover time thatis linear in the number of parallel walks. We demonstrate that an exponentialspeed-up is sometimes possible, but that some natural graphs allow only alogarithmic speed-up. A problem related to ours (in which the walks start fromsome probabilistic distribution on vertices) was previously studied in thecontext of space efficient algorithms for undirected s-t connectivity and ourresults yield, in certain cases, an improvement upon some of the earlierbounds.
direct_prompt: This paper investigates the efficiency of parallel stochastic processes by analyzing the performance of multiple independent random walks on various graph topologies. We specifically examine how increasing the number of walking agents influences key metrics such as the hitting time to a target node and the total cover time of the network. Our findings demonstrate that utilizing multiple random walks can reduce exploration times by a factor that often scales super-linearly with the number of agents, particularly in constrained or non-expandable structures. These results provide a theoretical foundation for optimizing decentralized search algorithms and enhancing the robustness of communication protocols in distributed systems.

title: Parametric Learning and Monte Carlo Optimization
human_text: This paper uncovers and explores the close relationship between Monte CarloOptimization of a parametrized integral (MCO), Parametric machine-Learning(PL), and `blackbox' or `oracle'-based optimization (BO). We make fourcontributions. First, we prove that MCO is mathematically identical to a broadclass of PL problems. This identity potentially provides a new applicationdomain for all broadly applicable PL techniques: MCO. Second, we introduceimmediate sampling, a new version of the Probability Collectives (PC) algorithmfor blackbox optimization. Immediate sampling transforms the original BOproblem into an MCO problem. Accordingly, by combining these first twocontributions, we can apply all PL techniques to BO. In our third contributionwe validate this way of improving BO by demonstrating that cross-validation andbagging improve immediate sampling. Finally, conventional MC and MCO proceduresignore the relationship between the sample point locations and the associatedvalues of the integrand; only the values of the integrand at those locationsare considered. We demonstrate that one can exploit the sample locationinformation using PL techniques, for example by forming a fit of the samplelocations to the associated values of the integrand. This provides anadditional way to apply PL techniques to improve MCO.
direct_prompt: Parametric learning provides a principled framework for representing complex stochastic systems through families of parameterized models. In this article, we investigate the interplay between parametric learning and Monte Carlo optimization, focusing on how sampling-based methods can be harnessed to improve parameter estimation and decision-making under uncertainty. We first formalize the problem of optimizing performance criteria defined as expectations with respect to unknown or intractable probability distributions. We then show how parametric models can be trained to approximate these distributions using data generated by Monte Carlo simulations. The resulting learning-optimization loop allows parameters to be updated in a way that directly targets the objective of interest, rather than merely fitting observed data. We analyze convergence properties of this loop under mild regularity conditions and demonstrate how variance reduction techniques can significantly accelerate learning. In particular, we highlight the role of importance sampling, control variates, and adaptive sampling schemes in stabilizing gradient-based updates. We also present a class of stochastic approximation algorithms that naturally arise from this perspective and relate them to existing methods in reinforcement learning and Bayesian computation.

title: Vector mesons from AdS/TC to the LHC
human_text: With the use of the AdS/CFT dictionary, a five-dimensional effectivedescription of dynamical electro-weak symmetry breaking with walking behavioris constructed. The minimal model contains only two new parameters, theconfinement scale and the effective coupling of the new strong sector. Thisparameter space is restricted by the precision electro-weak constraints and bythe requirement that the five-dimensional coupling be perturbative(corresponding to the large-N regime in four-dimensional language). Thelightest observable new states are a set of four nearly degenerate spin-1states with the same quantum numbers as the standard-model electro-weak gaugebosons, and masses in the few TeV range. Their decay rate is dominated bytwo-fermion final states. The number of pp -> mu mu and pp -> mu nu events isstudied as a function of the LHC integrated luminosity and of the two freeparameters. Discovery at the LHC is possible over a significant part of theallowed parameter space up to masses of 4 TeV already with 10/fm of integratedluminosity.
direct_prompt: This work explores the phenomenology of vector mesons arising from strongly coupled technicolor (TC) theories within the framework of the Anti-de Sitter/Technicolor (AdS/TC) correspondence. We construct a holographic model that captures essential features of the dynamical symmetry breaking responsible for generating vector resonances analogous to QCD ρ mesons. By mapping the five-dimensional gravitational dual to four-dimensional technicolor dynamics, we obtain predictions for the mass spectra and decay constants of these vector mesons. The implications of these states for collider experiments, particularly the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), are analyzed through their production cross sections and decay channels. We highlight characteristic signatures that distinguish TC vector mesons from other new physics scenarios, including deviations in dilepton and diboson invariant mass distributions. Our results suggest that current and future LHC data can place meaningful constraints on the parameter space of AdS/TC models, thereby providing a promising avenue for detecting or excluding technicolor-inspired composite states.

title: X-ray and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich scaling relations in galaxy clusters
human_text: [Abridged] We present an analysis of the scaling relations between X-rayproperties and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (SZ) parameters for a sample of 24 X-rayluminous galaxy clusters observed with Chandra and with measured SZ effect.These objects are in the redshift range 0.14--0.82 and have X-ray bolometricluminosity L>10^45 erg/s. We perform a spatially resolved spectral analysis andrecover the density, temperature and pressure profiles of the ICM, just relyingon the spherical symmetry of the cluster and the hydrostatic equilibriumhypothesis. We observe that the correlations among X-ray quantities only are inagreement with previous results obtained for samples of high-z X-ray luminousgalaxy clusters. On the relations involving SZ quantities, we obtain that theycorrelate with the gas temperature with a logarithmic slope significantlylarger than the predicted value from the self-similar model. The measuredscatter indicates, however, that the central Compton parameter y_0 is a proxyof the gas temperature at the same level of other X-ray quantities likeluminosity. Our results on the X-ray and SZ scaling relations show a tensionbetween the quantities more related to the global energy of the system (e.g.gas temperature, gravitating mass) and the indicators of the structure of theICM (e.g. gas density profile, central Compton parameter y_0), showing the mostsignificant deviations from the values of the slope predicted from theself-similar model in the L-T, L-M_{tot}, M_{gas}-T, y_0-T relations. When theslope is fixed to the self-similar value, these relations consistently show anegative evolution suggesting a scenario in which the ICM at higher redshifthas lower both X-ray luminosity and pressure in the central regions than theexpectations from self-similar model.
direct_prompt: This study investigates the scaling relations between X-ray observables and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (SZ) effect measurements in galaxy clusters, aiming to enhance the understanding of cluster physics and cosmology. We analyze a comprehensive sample of galaxy clusters using high-resolution X-ray data combined with SZ observations from recent microwave surveys. Our analysis focuses on key observables such as X-ray luminosity, temperature, and gas mass in relation to the SZ Compton-y parameter. We find that the scaling relations exhibit a high degree of correlation, with measured slopes and normalizations consistent with self-similar cluster evolution models after accounting for non-gravitational processes. The intrinsic scatter in these relations provides insights into complex astrophysical phenomena such as feedback, cooling, and dynamical state variations. Additionally, we explore the redshift dependence of the scaling relations, finding mild evolution consistent with theoretical predictions. These results reinforce the utility of combined X-ray and SZ measurements as robust tools for cluster mass estimation and cosmological parameter constraints. Our findings contribute to improving cluster-based methods for probing dark energy and large-scale structure formation in the universe.

title: Quantum spin liquid states in the two dimensional kagome  antiferromagnets, ZnxCu4-x(OD)6Cl2
human_text: A three-dimensional system of interacting spins typically develops staticlong-range order when it is cooled. If the spins are quantum (S = 1/2),however, novel quantum paramagnetic states may appear. The most highly soughtstate among them is the resonating valence bond (RVB) state in which every pairof neighboring quantum spins form entangled spin singlets (valence bonds) andthe singlets are quantum mechanically resonating amongst all the possiblehighly degenerate pairing states. Here we provide experimental evidence forsuch quantum paramagnetic states existing in frustrated antiferromagnets,ZnxCu4-x(OD)6Cl2, where the S = 1/2 magnetic Cu2+ moments form layers of atwo-dimensional kagome lattice. We find that in Cu4(OD)6Cl2, where distortedkagome planes are weakly coupled to each other, a dispersionless excitationmode appears in the magnetic excitation spectrum below ~ 20 K, whosecharacteristics resemble those of quantum spin singlets in a solid state, knownas a valence bond solid (VBS), that breaks translational symmetry. Dopingnonmagnetic Zn2+ ions reduces the distortion of the kagome lattice, and weakensthe interplane coupling but also dilutes the magnetic occupancy of the kagomelattice. The VBS state is suppressed and for ZnCu3(OD)6Cl2 where the kagomeplanes are undistorted and 90% occupied by the Cu2+ ions, the low energy spinfluctuations in the spin liquid phase become featureless.
direct_prompt: A three-dimensional system of interacting spins typically develops long-range magnetic order upon cooling, but quantum fluctuations in S=1/2 systems can lead to novel paramagnetic ground states. Among these, the resonating-valence-bond state represents a highly sought-after quantum spin liquid (QSL), characterized by entangled spin singlets resonating across degenerate configurations. The two-dimensional kagome lattice of corner-sharing triangles is theoretically predicted to host such QSL states due to strong geometric frustration in antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models. The family of compounds ZnxCu4-x(OD)6Cl2 provides experimental realizations of nearly ideal S=1/2 kagome antiferromagnets, with Cu2+ ions forming weakly coupled kagome layers and Zn2+ substitution tuning lattice distortion and magnetic dilution. Elastic and inelastic neutron scattering studies reveal that at low Zn doping, distorted kagome planes exhibit valence-bond-solid-like dispersionless excitations below ~20 K. Increasing Zn content reduces distortion and interplane coupling, suppressing the valence-bond-solid phase. For near-perfect kagome occupancy in ZnCu3(OD)6Cl2, low-energy spin fluctuations become continuum-like and featureless, indicative of a quantum spin liquid ground state with fractionalized excitations and no static order down to the lowest temperatures.

human_text: The second hand ticks slowly and methodically past each mark on the clock, like the warden on the last mile clacking his baton against each cell as he makes his rounds. Turning my head back to her, I gaze upon her radiant face one last time, a beacon of light amidst the gray, drab interior of the hospital room. " Is it time? " she asks. Her voice is shaky at first, but with every word she regains strength, the last syllable certain and unafraid. Time. Such a funny concept. As I sit beside her the seconds stretch themselves long and thin, but when I think about the years past - hot, sticky, passionate 16…over-the-moon in marriage 23…angry, confused, and empty 39 - the moments are flashes of light that appear and wink out of existence in the blink of an eye. " Yes, " my voice cracks. I was never as determined and driven as her. I look down, searching for a way to prolong the precious little time we have left. Suddenly I ask with conviction, " Tell me about the most favorite moment you had with me. " I can hardly bear to watch as she smiles, wincing from the effort. " Go, " she commands, placing her hand on my wrist beside her. With my other hand, I slowly wrap my fingers around the cord. A single teardrop falls from my bowed head as I pull the plug. I rise above the immediate sounding of alarms and beeps from the monitors, only to be met with a cloud of emotions. Anguish, despair, and hopelessness swirl around my head, blinding me. Suddenly I hear a voice, soft but filled with clarity. " Sixteen, " she whispers as she lays back, her mouth in a slight smile. human_text: Every day is the same. And all that self help, life coach, motivational quote bullshit is never, ever, going to save you from that. No one can convince you to be better. The spreadsheet awaiting his input at the office suddenly seemed like a foreign language he no longer wished to speak. He sat up, his heart pounding with a strange, rhythmic defiance. "I am not going back," he whispered, the words tasting like cool water in a desert. He walked to the kitchen and poured the stale coffee down the drain. Instead of his briefcase, he grabbed an old hiking pack from the back of the closet. He filled it with a few changes of clothes, a sketchbook he hadn't touched since college, and a sturdy pair of boots. His phone buzzed with a reminder for a 9:00 AM meeting, but he simply turned the device off. He left his keys on the kitchen counter, knowing he wouldn’t be needing them for a very long time. Stepping out onto the street, the city air felt different, charged with a sudden electricity. People rushed past him, their heads down, caught in the invisible currents of their own routines. title: Balance of forces in simulated bilayers
human_text: Two kinds of simulated bilayers are described and the results are reportedfor lateral tension and for partial contributions of intermolecular forces toit.Data for a widest possible range of areas per surfactant head, from tunnelformation through tensionless state, transition to floppy bilayer,to itsdisintegration, are reported and discussed. The significance of the tensionlessstate, is discussed. Conclusions: (1) the tensionless state is acoincidence;(2) the transition from extended to floppy bilayer occurs nearbyand has hallmarks of a phase transition (3) there is no theory of thattransition.(4)The lateral tension of the floppy bilayer scales with size; thatof the extended bilayer does not depend on size. direct_prompt: In this study, we investigate the balance of forces that governs the structural and dynamical properties of simulated lipid bilayers. Using atomistic and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we decompose the contributions from van der Waals, electrostatic, and steric interactions across a range of lipid compositions and thermodynamic conditions. We quantify how lateral pressure profiles, surface tension, and membrane curvature arise from these underlying microscopic forces. Particular attention is given to the coupling between lipid packing, hydration forces, and headgroup electrostatics in establishing bilayer stability and thickness. We demonstrate that subtle changes in lipid tail saturation, cholesterol content, and ionic strength lead to measurable shifts in the force balance that correlate with emergent bilayer mechanical properties.

title: Experimental studies on vacancy induced ferromagnetism in undoped TiO2
human_text: Room temperature ferromagnetism is observed in undoped TiO2 films depositedon Si substrates using pulsed laser deposition (PLD). The ferromagneticproperties of the samples depend on the oxygen partial pressure during the PLDsynthesis. The appearance of higher binding energy component (HBEC) in theoxygen 1s core peak from x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) suggests thepresence of oxygen vacancies in these samples. The amount of oxygen during thesynthesis determines the vacancy concentration in the samples which is directlyrelated to the magnetic behavior of the samples. The magnetic moment decreaseswith oxygen vacancy concentration in the samples. Valence band measurementswere performed to study the electronic structure of both stoichometric andreduced TiO2. The analyses show the presence of Ti 3d band near the Fermi levelin reduced TiO2 samples. These bands are otherwise empty in stoichiometric TiO2and reside in the conduction band which makes them unobservable by XPS. Theexistence of this Ti 3d band near the Fermi level can possibly lead to Stonersplitting of the band.
direct_prompt: This study investigates the emergence of ferromagnetism in undoped titanium dioxide (TiO2) arising from intrinsic oxygen vacancies. Utilizing a combination of controlled annealing processes and vacuum treatments, we systematically induced and characterized vacancy concentrations within TiO2 thin films. Magnetic measurements reveal a clear correlation between the density of oxygen vacancies and the magnitude of ferromagnetic ordering at room temperature. Structural analyses using X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy confirm that the ferromagnetism is not attributable to secondary phases or magnetic impurities. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy further substantiates the formation of vacancy-related defect states responsible for magnetic moments. The experimental results are supported by density functional theory calculations, which indicate that localized electron spins associated with oxygen vacancies mediate ferromagnetic coupling. Our findings demonstrate that intrinsic defects alone can produce robust ferromagnetism in undoped TiO2, opening avenues for defect-engineered spintronic materials.

title: Comprehensive simulations of superhumps
human_text: (Abridged) We use 3D SPH calculations with higher resolution, as well as withmore realistic viscosity and sound-speed prescriptions than previous work toexamine the eccentric instability which underlies the superhump phenomenon insemi-detached binaries. We illustrate the importance of the two-armed spiralmode in the generation of superhumps. Differential motions in the fluid disccause converging flows which lead to strong spiral shocks once each superhumpcycle. The dissipation associated with these shocks powers the superhump. Wecompare 2D and 3D results, and conclude that 3D simulations are necessary tofaithfully simulate the disc dynamics. We ran our simulations for unprecedenteddurations, so that an eccentric equilibrium is established except at high massratios where the growth rate of the instability is very low. Our improvedsimulations give a closer match to the observed relationship between superhumpperiod excess and binary mass ratio than previous numerical work. The observedblack hole X-ray transient superhumpers appear to have systematically lowerdisc precession rates than the cataclysmic variables. This could be due tohigher disc temperatures and thicknesses. The modulation in total viscousdissipation on the superhump period is overwhelmingly from the region of thedisc within the 3:1 resonance radius. As the eccentric instability develops,the viscous torques are enhanced, and the disc consequently adjusts to a newequilibrium state, as suggested in the thermal-tidal instability model. Wequantify this enhancement in the viscosity, which is ~10 per cent for q=0.08.We characterise the eccentricity distributions in our accretion discs, and showthat the entire body of the disc partakes in the eccentricity.
direct_prompt: We present a suite of three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations designed to investigate the origin, structure, and evolution of superhumps in accretion discs of cataclysmic variable systems. The simulations employ a high-resolution, grid-based code with an isothermal equation of state, including full tidal forces from a Roche-lobe filling secondary. We systematically explore a wide range of mass ratios, disc viscosities, and mass-transfer rates to identify the conditions under which superhump modulations are excited and sustained. Our results confirm that superhumps are associated with the growth of an eccentric, precessing disc mode excited near the 3:1 outer Lindblad resonance. We demonstrate that the precession rate and superhump period excess correlate strongly with the mass ratio and disc radius, in good agreement with observational constraints. The simulations reproduce both positive and negative superhumps by varying the disc tilt and vertical structure. We find that the amplitude and stability of superhumps depend sensitively on the adopted viscosity prescription and the strength of tidal torques. Disc eccentricity exhibits quasi-periodic cycles of growth and damping, naturally producing the observed evolution of superhump amplitudes over a superoutburst. Synthetic light curves derived from the simulations match the observed morphology of superhump waveforms, including their characteristic asymmetry and harmonic content. Our parameter survey constrains the region of mass ratio and disc size space in which persistent superhumps can exist. We discuss the implications of our results for using superhumps as probes of binary parameters, particularly mass ratios in faint or distant systems. Finally, we outline how these comprehensive simulations can guide future observational campaigns and inform more realistic models including magnetic fields and.

title: Precise Timing of the X-ray Pulsar 1E 1207.4-5209: A Steady Neutron Star  Weakly Magnetized at Birth
human_text: We analyze all X-ray timing data on 1E 1207.4-5209 in supernova remnant PKS1209-51/52 gathered in 2000-2005, and find a highly stable rotation withP=424.130451(4) ms and period derivative of (9.6 +/- 9.4)E-17 s/s. This refutesprevious claims of large timing irregularities in these data. In the dipolespin-down formalism, the 2-sigma upper limit on period derivative implies anenergy loss rate < 1.5E32 ergs/s, surface magnetic field strength B_p < 3.5E11G, and characteristic age tau > 24 Myr. This tau exceeds the remnant age by 3orders of magnitude, requiring that the pulsar was born spinning at its presentperiod. The X-ray luminosity of 1E 1207.4-5209, L(bol) ~= 2E33 ergs/s at 2 kpc,exceeds its spin-down energy loss, implying that L(bol) derives from residualcooling, and perhaps partly from accretion of supernova debris. direct_prompt: The isolated X-ray pulsar 1E 1207.4-5209, located in the supernova remnant PKS 1209-51/52, exhibits distinctive timing properties that provide crucial insights into neutron star birth and evolution. We report on high-precision timing observations obtained from multiple X-ray observatories, enabling an unprecedentedly accurate measurement of the pulsar’s spin period and its derivative. Our analysis reveals an exceptionally stable rotation with a very small spin-down rate, indicating a weak surface dipole magnetic field on the order of 10^11 G. This low magnetic field strength contrasts with typical young neutron stars, suggesting that 1E 1207.4-5209 was born with a comparatively weak magnetic field. The timing results, combined with spectral and thermal emission characteristics, support a scenario where magnetic field evolution is minimal over the pulsar’s estimated age. These findings have significant implications for the understanding of neutron star magnetic field generation mechanisms and provide evidence that not all neutron stars are born as strong magnetized objects. Ultimately, this study advances the picture of neutron star birth properties, highlighting a category of steady, weakly magnetized X-ray pulsars.

title: Star-Formation in Low Radio Luminosity AGN from the Sloan Digital Sky  Survey
human_text: We investigate faint radio emission from low- to high-luminosity ActiveGalactic Nuclei (AGN) selected from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). Theirradio properties are inferred by co-adding large ensembles of radio imagecut-outs from the FIRST survey, as almost all of the sources are individuallyundetected. We correlate the median radio flux densities against a range ofother sample properties, including median values for redshift, [OIII]luminosity, emission line ratios, and the strength of the 4000A break. Wedetect a strong trend for sources that are actively undergoing star-formationto have excess radio emission beyond the ~10^28 ergs/s/Hz level found forsources without any discernible star-formation. Furthermore, this additionalradio emission correlates well with the strength of the 4000A break in theoptical spectrum, and may be used to assess the age of the star-formingcomponent. We examine two subsamples, one containing the systems with emissionline ratios most like star-forming systems, and one with the sources that havecharacteristic AGN ratios. This division also separates the mechanismresponsible for the radio emission (star-formation vs. AGN). For both cases wefind a strong, almost identical, correlation between [OIII] and radioluminosity, with the AGN sample extending toward lower, and the star-formationsample toward higher luminosities. A clearer separation between the twosubsamples is seen as function of the central velocity dispersion of the hostgalaxy. For systems with similar redshifts and velocity dispersions, thestar-formation subsample is brighter than the AGN in the radio by an order ofmagnitude. This underlines the notion that the radio emission in star-formingsystems can dominate the emission associated with the AGN.
direct_prompt: This study investigates the relationship between star-formation activity and low radio luminosity in active galactic nuclei (AGN) using data from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). We select a sample of AGN characterized by low radio power to explore whether their host galaxies exhibit ongoing star-formation. Our analysis combines optical emission line diagnostics with radio continuum measurements to disentangle the contributions from AGN and star-formation processes. We find that a significant fraction of low radio luminosity AGN reside in galaxies with measurable star-formation rates. The correlation between radio luminosity and star-formation indicators suggests that the radio emission in these sources is partly driven by star-formation rather than solely by AGN jets or lobes. Moreover, the host galaxy properties imply that the interplay between black hole activity and star-formation is complex and possibly linked to the galaxy’s evolutionary stage. We observe that the star-formation rates tend to decrease with increasing AGN radio power, highlighting a potential feedback mechanism. Our results highlight the importance of careful multiwavelength analysis when interpreting radio emission in low-luminosity AGN. We also discuss how selection effects in the SDSS sample could influence the observed trends. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the co-evolution of galaxies and their central black holes, especially in the regime of weak radio AGN activity. Future work using deeper radio observations will be crucial to refine these conclusions and explore the faint end of the AGN population.

title: Matter-wave interference in s-wave and p-wave Fermi condensates
human_text: We discuss the time evolution and matter-wave interference of Fermicondensates on the BEC side of Feshbach resonances for s and p-wavesuperfluids, upon release from harmonic traps. In swave systems, where theorder parameter is a complex scalar, we find that the interference patternsdepend on the relative phase of the order parameters of the condensates. Inp-wave systems involving the mixture of two-hyperfine states, we show that theinterference pattern exhibits a polarization effect depending on the relativeorientation of the two vector order parameters. Lastly, we also point out thatp-wave Fermi condensates exhibit an anisotropic expansion, reflecting thespatial anisotropy of the underlying interaction between fermions and theorbital nature of the vector order parameter. Potential applications of ourresults include systems of ultra-cold atoms that exhibit p-wave Feshbachresonances such as 6Li or 40K.
direct_prompt: This study investigates matter-wave interference phenomena in ultracold Fermi condensates exhibiting both s-wave and p-wave pairing symmetries. By analyzing the coherence properties and phase dynamics of these condensates, we reveal key differences in interference patterns arising from the orbital angular momentum of the Cooper pairs. Our theoretical framework extends conventional treatments of s-wave superfluidity to incorporate the anisotropic character of p-wave interactions, highlighting novel collective modes and interference signatures. Numerical simulations demonstrate how tuning interaction parameters and external potentials affect the visibility and fringe spacing in matter-wave interferometry experiments. These findings provide new insights into the quantum behavior of unconventional Fermi superfluids and offer guidance for future experimental exploration of p-wave pairing in ultracold atomic gases.

title: A new spinfoam vertex for quantum gravity
human_text: We introduce a new spinfoam vertex to be used in models of 4d quantum gravitybased on SU(2) and SO(4) BF theory plus constraints. It can be seen as theconventional vertex of SU(2) BF theory, the 15j symbol, in a particular basisconstructed using SU(2) coherent states. This basis makes the geometricinterpretation of the variables transparent: they are the vectors normal to thetriangles within each tetrahedron. We study the condition under which thesestates can be considered semiclassical, and we show that the semiclassical onesdominate the evaluation of quantum correlations. Finally, we describe how theconstraints reducing BF to gravity can be directly written in terms of the newvariables, and how the semiclassicality of the states might improveunderstanding the correct way to implement the constraints.
direct_prompt: We present a novel construction for the spinfoam vertex amplitude within the framework of loop quantum gravity. This model addresses specific mathematical inconsistencies found in the implementation of simplicity constraints for Lorentzian manifolds. By introducing an alternative mapping between the SU(2) and SL(2,C) representations, we derive a modified vertex that ensures a more consistent semiclassical limit. Our analysis confirms that the large-spin asymptotic behavior of the amplitude accurately reproduces the Regge action, providing a direct link to classical general relativity. These findings offer a refined dynamical foundation for calculating transition amplitudes in non-perturbative quantum cosmology.

title: Bimodal AGNs in Bimodal Galaxies
human_text: By their star content, the galaxies split out into a red and a bluepopulation; their color index peaked around u-r=2.5 or u-r=1, respectively,quantifies the ratio of the blue stars newly formed from cold galactic gas, tothe redder ones left over by past generations. On the other hand, uponaccreting substantial gas amounts the central massive black holes energizeactive galactic nuclei (AGNs); here we investigate whether these show asimilar, and possibly related, bimodal partition as for current accretionactivity relative to the past. To this aim we use an updated semianalyticmodel; based on Monte Carlo simulations, this follows with a large statisticsthe galaxy assemblage, the star generations and the black hole accretions inthe cosmological framework over the redshift span from z=10 to z=0. We test oursimulations for yielding in close detail the observed split of galaxies into ared, early and a blue, late population. We find that the black hole accretionactivities likewise give rise to two source populations: early, bright quasarsand later, dimmer AGNs. We predict for their Eddington parameter $\lambda_E$ --the ratio of the current to the past black hole accretions -- a bimodaldistribution; the two branches sit now under $\lambda_E \approx 0.01$ (mainlycontributed by low-luminosity AGNs) and around $\lambda_E \approx 0.3-1$. While Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs) are widely considered to be the primary drivers of this evolutionary transition, the precise relationship between black hole accretion modes and host galaxy properties remains a subject of intense debate. In this study, we utilize a comprehensive multi-wavelength dataset to investigate whether AGNs themselves exhibit a parallel bimodality that mirrors their host environments. Our results reveal two clearly defined populations of AGNs: high-excitation sources predominantly found in blue, gas-rich galaxies and low-excitation sources residing in massive, red, early-type galaxies. We demonstrate that the radiative efficiency of these nuclei is intrinsically linked to the specific star formation rate of the host, suggesting that a shared gas reservoir regulates both nuclear and galactic-scale growth. This observed duality in AGN behavior provides strong evidence for a feedback model where different accretion mechanisms facilitate the crossing of the green valley and the subsequent maintenance of the red sequence. Ultimately, our findings suggest that the co-evolution of supermassive black holes and galaxies is a synchronized process governed by the availability of cold gas and large-scale environmental triggers.

title: The effect of magnetic fields on the formation of circumstellar discs  around young stars
human_text: We present first results of our simulations of magnetic fields in theformation of single and binary stars using a recently developed method forincorporating Magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) into the Smoothed ParticleHydrodynamics (SPH) method. An overview of the method is presented beforediscussing the effect of magnetic fields on the formation of circumstellardiscs around young stars. We find that the presence of magnetic fields duringthe disc formation process can lead to significantly smaller and less massivediscs which are much less prone to gravitational instability. Similarly in thecase of binary star formation we find that magnetic fields, overall, suppressfragmentation. However these effects are found to be largely driven by magneticpressure. The relative importance of magnetic tension is dependent on theorientation of the field with respect to the rotation axis, but can, with theright orientation, lead to a dilution of the magnetic pressure-drivensuppression of fragmentation.
direct_prompt: Circumstellar discs around young stars are expected to form naturally from the conservation of angular momentum during the gravitational collapse of rotating molecular cloud cores. However, theoretical models incorporating magnetic fields reveal that efficient magnetic braking can remove excess angular momentum, potentially suppressing the formation of rotationally supported discs. This phenomenon, known as the magnetic braking catastrophe, results in significantly smaller and less massive discs in magnetized environments compared to purely hydrodynamic simulations. Non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic effects, such as ambipolar diffusion and the Hall effect, as well as misalignment between magnetic fields and rotation axes, can mitigate braking efficiency and enable the emergence of Keplerian discs with radii of tens to hundreds of AU. Numerical simulations further demonstrate that magnetic pressure and tension contribute to reduced fragmentation, yielding more stable disc structures less prone to gravitational instability.

title: Evidence for a planetary companion around a nearby young star
human_text: We report evidence for a planetary companion around the nearby young star HD70573. The star is a G type dwarf located at a distance of 46 pc with ageestimation between 20 and 300 Myrs. We carried out spectroscopic observationsof this star with FEROS at the 2.2 m MPG/ESO telescope at La Silla. Ourspectroscopic analysis yields a spectral type of G1-1.5V and an age of about100 Myrs. Variations in stellar radial velocity of HD 70573 have been monitoredsince December 2003 until January 2007. The velocity accuracy of FEROS withinthis period is about 10 m/s. HD 70573 shows a radial velocity variation with aperiod of 852 +/- 12 days and a semi-amplitude of 149 +/- 6 m/s. The period ofthis variation is significantly longer than its rotational period, which is 3.3days. Based on the analysis of the Ca II K emission line, Halpha and Teffvariation as stellar activity indicators as well as the lack of a correlationbetween the bisector velocity span and the radial velocity, we can exclude therotational modulation and non-radial pulsations as the source of thelong-period radial velocity variation. Thus, the presence of a low-masscompanion around the star provides the best explanation for the observed radialvelocity variation. Assuming a primary mass m1=1.0 +/- 0.1 Msun for the hoststar, we calculated a minimum mass of the companion m2sini of 6.1 Mjup, whichlies in the planetary mass regime, and an orbital semi-major axis of 1.76 AU.The orbit of the planet has an eccentricity of e=0.4. The planet discoveryaround the young star HD 70573 gives an important input for the study of debrisdisks around young stars and their relation to the presence of planets.
direct_prompt: Evidence for a planetary companion around a nearby young star is presented based on a combination of high-precision radial velocity monitoring, direct imaging, and astrometric constraints. Our target is a nearby (d ≈ 25 pc), solar-type pre-main sequence star with an estimated age of 50–100 Myr, making it an ideal laboratory for studying early planetary system evolution. Using high-resolution spectroscopic observations spanning 6 years, we detect a coherent radial velocity signal with a semi-amplitude of 38 ± 3 m s⁻¹ and a period of 420 ± 15 days. We perform a detailed analysis of stellar activity indicators, including line bisectors, chromospheric emission, and photometric variability, and find no correlation with the observed radial velocity variations. High-contrast adaptive optics imaging excludes the presence of stellar-mass companions at projected separations larger than 10 au down to the hydrogen-burning limit. Combining the radial velocity and imaging data, we derive a minimum mass for the companion of 2.8 ± 0.4 M_Jup at a semi-major axis of 1.2 ± 0.1 au. Astrometric measurements from space-based observatories show marginal, but consistent, evidence for a reflex motion compatible with the radial velocity solution. We explore dynamical stability and find that the proposed configuration is compatible with long-term orbital stability given the star’s estimated mass and age. The probability that the signal arises from stellar activity, an unseen binary companion, or instrumental effects is quantitatively assessed and found to be less than 1%. We interpret the detected object as a young Jovian planet in an orbit analogous to that of the inner giant planets in the Solar System.

title: Area laws in quantum systems: mutual information and correlations
human_text: The holographic principle states that on a fundamental level the informationcontent of a region should depend on its surface area rather than on itsvolume. This counterintuitive idea which has its roots in the nonextensivenature of black-hole entropy serves as a guiding principle in the search forthe fundamental laws of Planck-scale physics. In this paper we show that asimilar phenomenon emerges from the established laws of classical and quantumphysics: the information contained in part of a system in thermal equilibriumobeys an area law. While the maximal information per unit area dependsclassically only on the number of microscopic degrees of freedom, it maydiverge as the inverse temperature in quantum systems. A rigorous relationbetween area laws and correlations is established and their explicit behavioris revealed for a large class of quantum many-body states beyond equilibriumsystems.
direct_prompt: The area law for entanglement entropy characterizes the scaling behavior of quantum information in many-body systems, suggesting that correlations are often concentrated along the boundaries of subsystems. This article examines the extension of this principle to mutual information, which provides a comprehensive measure of both classical and quantum correlations in mixed and thermal states. We analyze the fundamental connection between the exponential decay of correlation functions and the emergence of an area law for the total correlation between disjoint regions. By considering systems with local interactions, we demonstrate that the mutual information remains proportional to the interface area, thereby limiting the entanglement complexity of the global state. These results offer a rigorous framework for understanding the information-theoretic properties of quantum phases and justify the success of boundary-based numerical methods like tensor networks.

human_text: We present a ground based photometry of the low-temperature contact binary BBPeg. This period increase of BB Pegcan be interpreted in terms of the mass transfer 2.4 x 10^{-8} Ms yr^{-1} fromthe less massive to the more massive component. The physical parameters havebeen determined as Mc = 1.42 Ms, Mh = 0.53 Ms, Rc = 1.29 Rs, Rh = 0.83 Rs, Lc =1.86 Ls, and Lh = 0.94 Ls through simultaneous solution of light and of theradial velocity curves. The orbital parameters of the third body, that orbitsthe contact system in an eccentric orbit, were obtained from the periodvariation analysis. The system is compared to the similar binaries in theHertzsprung-Russell and Mass-Radius diagram.
